text:
anika: Quick sync on prepaid slabs + route-level quotas. We keep getting asks for "buy X tokens and never worry about throttles on endpoint Y". Need guardrails before we spec the pricing page.

mira: Agree. Major concerns: operational visibility, accounting for cross-route cache hits, and preventing customers from buying an island of capacity that starves others.

kevin: Sales pitch wants two products: 1) Prepaid slab (buy compute units, apply to account), 2) Route-bound slab (prepaid but reserved for a specific route). Route-bound will be a competitive win for high QPS customers.

legal_liz: From a contract standpoint we must avoid language that implies capacity guarantees unless we include explicit SLA credits. We can offer "priority consumption" but with clear non-guarantee and overage rates.

ops_sam: Operational constraints: we can implement soft-reservation at the router layer + strict enforcement at serving layer. If route-bound slab empties, fallback to account slab, then to shared pool with throttling.

anika: That fallback flow sounds right. Can we show it on the pricing page? Need to be explicit so sales can't promise unlimited.

mira: Suggested product config (proto):

```yaml
pricing:
  slab:
    id: prepaid_compute_v1
    unit: compute_unit
    purchase_options:
      - sku: slab-small
        units: 25000
        price_usd: 2500
      - sku: slab-medium
        units: 100000
        price_usd: 9000
    applies_to: account
  route_slab:
    id: route_reserved_v1
    unit: compute_unit
    reservation_policy:
      per_route_cap_pct: 0.8   # cannot reserve more than 80% of route's projected baseline
      fallback_order: [route, account_slab, shared_pool]
      expiry_days: 365
      refund_policy: no_refund
```

mira: Key enforcement knobs: per-route cap percent, expiration, and mandatory billing tag propagation for every request so we can attribute usage.

kevin: Sales asks for an "auto-topup" option when a slab drops below 10%. Need to confirm we can support it without surprising invoices.

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-2201: "Slab auto-topup options and invoice preview feature" assigned to billing-team, due=2025-05-09.

legal_liz: Contract snippet proposal: "Prepaid Slabs are a purchased credit balance applied to compute consumption. Prepaid Slabs are non-refundable, expire per the purchased product terms, and do not constitute a capacity or latency commitment unless explicitly stated in a separate SLA addendum. Overages beyond Prepaid Slabs will be billed at published overage rates."

anika: Launch gating checklist brainstorm:
  - Billing tagging works end-to-end (test matrix across SDK + API + Console)
  - Console shows available slab balance per route + account
  - Alerts on slab utilization >75% and >95%
  - Fallback flow validated with chaos tests (route reserve depleted mid-flight)
  - Contract language approved by Legal
  - Pricing page copy reviewed by Marketing

mira: Also add metrics: pooled capacity impact <4% for first 3 months, p95 latency change <8% on affected routes. If exceeded, pause new route reservations.

kevin: For commercial flexibility propose a "trial holdback": when sales offers route-bound slab as a demo, we permit a time-limited holdback (max 30d) before full reservation kicks in, so ops can validate.

ops_sam: Implementation note: need a console toggle per-customer to enable route reservations + a way to forcibly drain reserved units for safety (emergency reclaim).

anika: UX ask: on purchase flow include an explicit checkbox: "I understand reserved units are non-refundable and may be reclaimed in emergency events." That reduces disputes.

legal_liz: Good. Also require an internal escalation path for requests to make route reservations indefinite or to add SLA. Those need VP approval and a written addendum.

mira: I'll draft the product spec and the enforcement contract language. Will include example UI screenshots and the test-case matrix. Target: draft ready by next Tue.

kevin: I'll coordinate with finance to get recommended MSRP and suggested discount bands for slabs.

billing-bot: BILL-2201 updated: added fields invoice_preview=true, auto_topup_flagging.

anika: Great. Let's review the draft spec on Tuesday. If anyone wants to add edge-cases (multi-tenant routes, embeddings-heavy traffic, model-quantization credits), drop them into BILL-2201.

kevin: +1

ops_sam: I'll add chaos test scenarios to PR infra testbed and link to BILL-2201.
